rules.title: Horizon Zero Dawn
config: # BCD's recommended settings for Horizon Zero Dawn.
# Reset to Recommended, at the bottom of the game's settings, brings them back.
notes: Horizon Zero Dawn (Complete Edition, GOG or Steam), still being brought
up: the list for build 471's test. Its shaders keep their constant
buffers, samplers and textures in register spaces 6 and 8, which build
466 refused (the game then crashed); MFC ships with build 468. Build 469
drew the first frame and hung (a pipeline without a pixel shader, fixed
in 471); DXGI now lists the virtual monitor's own modes, as user32 does,
so the game can pick this screen's resolution. Build 471 reached the
language menu at 56 FPS with no input at all: no window was foreground,
so its raw keyboard and mouse input went nowhere, and it reads its pad
only through Windows.Gaming.Input; build 475's two switches cover both.
On build 475 (2026-10-09 16:20) the game played for seven minutes, then
stopped with an "Error" box when its settings menu was refused a
pipeline: the converter refused ~4,900 of its shaders with code 4 (they
read a "t4-unbounded" range), each of them again for every pipeline.
Build 477's switches retry those with sized ranges, remember what stays
refused, and hand the game a placeholder instead of a failure; Wine's
"controller_get_User stub" line (12,747 of them, the game asks every
frame) is silenced. On build 479 (19:44) the retried shaders converted,
but the game stopped with "Error" at start: the orphan-lock reaper had
released two locks whose owners were alive (one on 475 too). Build 480's
line lets it release only locks a live thread has stamped. On build 480
(20:28) the game reached play, and iOS closed it two seconds in at
8,189 MB: in its menu it had created 52,570 pipelines, and their 23,045
shader libraries stayed in memory although a few thousand are drawn; the
image was corrupted from the first gameplay frame, when the game began to
clear rectangles of its targets and the whole targets were cleared. Build
481's list lets a pipeline's libraries go until its first draw, clears only
the rectangles, puts the game's memory in the swap file as Red Dead
Redemption 2's list does (broad, from 1 MB), and leaves out pso-warm, whose
queue held 24,570 pipelines (and their libraries) when the game closed.
On build 481 (21:52, 21:55) the game played without closing, but its
characters, which it skins in compute shaders, came out with missing
faces, missing hair or collapsed to spikes every few frames, with
gpu-sync = 1 as without it. Build 483's list adds two diagnostics:
skin-check logs those draws, the dispatches that wrote their vertices and
copies of the vertices themselves; view-census names buffer views that
fall back or are cut short. d3d12-typed-uav-load = 1 changed nothing
(481, 23:19). Build 484's list is one test of every candidate the
research left at once, each its own line: the game reads OPTIONS1, so
d3d12-wave-ops = 0 gives it shaders without wave intrinsics; raw and
structured buffer views also carry a texture view (typed reads of them
read zeros otherwise); R32 typed UAVs get ShaderAtomic; FEX orders vector
and memcpy accesses as x86 does and ignores the volatile metadata of
concrt140.dll and mfc140.dll. If the characters come out whole, the lines
are halved to find the one that matters; skin-check stays on either way.
None of them helped (484, 2026-10-10 07:32), so build 485's list drops
them again. Its skinning dispatches gave the same vertex a different
extreme depending on which of the game's two upload heaps the frame
used, so the list now starts typed buffer views at the 16-byte boundary
Apple's converter documents (a bone palette then has no padding
elements), and skin-check traces whole frames, keeps the vertex shaders
of meshes skinned there, dumps the compute skinning's data and compares
what the GPU read with what the CPU had written. On build 485 (09:35)
the characters came out whole: the dumped skinning matched a recompute
vertex for vertex, and the GPU read exactly the CPU's bytes. Plants and
lighting still flicker, and a small view two compute passes read every
frame started 4 bytes past a 16-byte boundary in some frames, so build
486's list starts every typed view exactly at its first element where a
probe shows the GPU reads such textures right, and drops the skinning
diagnostics (view-census stays: it counts the views that keep an offset).
On build 486 (11:52) nothing changed: the probe showed the GPU reads such
a texture from its start rounded down to 16 bytes, and whole walls,
trees and plants went missing for one frame every few seconds, at the
moments the depth pyramid the game culls with read back near depths.
Build 487's list gives typed views of upload memory that start off a
16-byte boundary an aligned copy of their bytes (typed-view-shadow),
holds a queue's wait until the work it waits for is committed
(fence-strict), and logs every frame's draws and the pyramid as the GPU
wrote it (vis-trace). Build 489's list adds desc-guard, which logs the
game rewriting a descriptor that a batch still running on the GPU uses
(another one-frame cause: that draw reads another object's data).
Build 490's list keeps the game's two 32 MB readback buffers, where the
GPU writes the depth pyramid the CPU culls with, on Metal's own memory
instead of the file-backed swap tier (readback-swap = 0); vis-trace now
also compares every pyramid readback with the GPU's own copy. Build
491's list reads a table's single constant buffers when the draw is
recorded, as NVIDIA's driver and vkd3d-proton do (static-cbv): with
vkd3d-proton, Horizon Zero Dawn Remastered's foliage flicker stops when
that is extended to every such constant buffer. On build 491 the game
rendered without a fault (19:28). Two runs then showed what matters: the
list without fence-strict, static-cbv, readback-swap and the trace
diagnostics stayed clean (19:58), and without typed-view-shadow the
vanishing came back (20:01). That list is version 15. Build 494's list
(version 16) adds two lines for frame rate (493, 2026-10-11): our
runtime's log lines no longer go through OutputDebugString, whose
exception and server request cost ~0.5 ms a line, and the census frames
that froze the game for 1.5-2 s every ~10 s in its first minutes are
off (quiet-log); the server names the shader-cache files it opens with
one call instead of realpath, which kept it busy on a performance core
in the menu (MADEIRA_SRV_FGETPATH).
Version 17 (2026-10-23): env.MADEIRA_MFC_DOCK = 1 (build 591). The same game started through Madeira Dock fails at once: an iPad17,3
(Send Log TH3BJ8, build 580, 2026-10-22) "[dll-missing] ... L\"mfc140.dll\" status=c0000135" (L30641), "import_dll Library mfc140.dll
(which is needed by ...\Horizon Zero Dawn\HorizonZeroDawn.exe) not found" (L30642), "loader_init ... Importing dlls ... failed, status
c0000135" (L31875), "[dock-game-end]" (L33392). A Dock session runs Wine's explorer.exe from the aarch64 bundle, so the Microsoft VC++
overlay, which also links mfc140.dll and mfc140u.dll, is never applied to it. The switch links the two MFC DLLs into such a session
only, where this game cannot get past its imports today (the Dock logs of Horizon Zero Dawn Remastered, which imports no MFC, are
not this game); a start that already has the overlay is not changed by it. Not tried on a
device yet.

rules.title: Horizon Forbidden West
config: # BCD's recommended settings for Horizon Forbidden West.
# Reset to Recommended, at the bottom of the game's settings, brings them back.
notes: Horizon Forbidden West (Complete Edition, Steam), still being brought up:
the list of build 517's eleventh try (2026-10-13 10:55), changed for build
526's test. The game needs AVX. Memory it frees is released at once (with
the free delay it asked for the same addresses again and looped), and its
programs run from their own image, which leaves the JIT pool room. Its
memory goes to the swap file from 64 KB, and it sees a 3 GB video-memory
budget with budget events (a smaller one left it on a black screen).
Horizon Zero Dawn's typed-view alignment and aligned copies keep the image
right: without the copies, vegetation shot into the sky (525, 12:44).
Version 1 had the copies off because their table filled in seconds and
every entry was compared at every submission (10:14); since 526 the table
holds 262,144 copies, gives idle ones to new views and compares only
recent ones. Render passes stay open across lists. Discarded targets are
loaded again (version 1 skipped the load; FSR 3 frame generation then
showed black squares, 525). Our log lines skip OutputDebugString and the
census frames; shader libraries wait for a pipeline's first draw; guest
threads run at the efficiency QoS; the thread samplers are off and Wine's
fixme lines are quiet. On 525 with FSR 3 frame generation the game showed
28-35 frames a second (about half of them generated).
Version 3 (build 528's test): on 526 the vegetation still went into the sky
with every offset view copied, so 528 refreshes all the copies once a
present, and this list turns on the census and skin-check diagnostics that
found Horizon Zero Dawn's view (quiet-log off: it hides their lines). A
diagnostic run: slower, with short freezes.
Version 4 (build 529's test): on 528 the GPU read exactly what the CPU wrote
(skin-check), but 1,789 of the game's typed views were R32G32B32 (float3),
which Metal has no texture-buffer format for; they fell back to plain
buffers that a typed load sees as no texture. typed-view-rgb32 gives them a
16-byte-element copy. The diagnostics are gone again and quiet-log is back.
Version 5 (build 534): FSR 3 frame generation's black squares came from its
inpainting pyramid, created with MipLevels 0 (the full chain) but made with
one level; its mip levels were written into FSR's motion-vector fields.
mip0-full gives such textures their full chain (build 533: the squares are
gone).

rules.title: Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart
config: # BCD's recommended settings for Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart.
# Reset to Recommended, at the bottom of the game's settings, brings them back.
notes: Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart (Steam 1895880), not yet seen running: a Discord
tester's first try on build 531 (2026-10-14, iPhone 15 Pro Max) ended a few
seconds after RiftApart.exe started, with AVX off and the standard list. Like
the other Nixxes ports (Ghost of Tsushima, the Horizon games) it is a D3D12
game with DirectStorage, so it starts from Horizon Forbidden West's general
lines: AVX and an NVIDIA GPU reported, the swap file and video-memory budget,
frees released at once, programs run from their own image (its 113 MB
program left a shrunken JIT pool), float3 typed views copied, MipLevels 0
textures given their full chain, the frame-rate and quiet-log switches and the
pad lines. Left out: Decima's typed-view alignment and copies, rp-carry, and
eco (on HFW it kept the game on the efficiency cores).
Version 2 (owner's 12 GB phone, build 549, log RiftApart.exe 2026-10-15
22:07:15): the intro videos played, then a black screen and an access
violation at rip 0. The game makes each 4 GB arena with an 8 GB probe it
releases at once; after four arenas no 8 GB hole was left below the
emulator's arena, the fifth probe failed and the game called a NULL.
env.MADEIRA_JUMBO_HALF gives such a probe the 4 GB it keeps.
Version 3 (owner's phone, build 550, log RiftApart.exe 2026-10-15
23:21:48: the game opened and ran without a crash): before it, R6025 at
10-43 s, because the guest band below 0x7400000000 was full and an image
(secur32.dll) or an allocation found no room, while 8 GB of the band sat
in the V8 cage holdback no Chromium asks for here.
env.MADEIRA_CAGE_RELEASE hands it over when the band runs out (as a Dock
launch does); jumbo-half then gave three probes their 4 GB.
Version 4 (owner's phone, build 553, logs RiftApart.exe 2026-10-16 10:43:45
and 10:45:10, R6025 again): v3 left out env.LC_ALL, which the 23:21:48 run
also had. Without it Wine takes the phone's language (tr-TR) as the user
locale; the game's main thread loads the Turkish OEM code page (857) and
throws an unhandled C++ exception on the next line, in both runs as on
550 22:49:00. LC_ALL = en_US.UTF-8 gives Wine an English locale for this game.
Version 5 (owner's phone, build 555, log RiftApart.exe 2026-10-16 12:32:19: the
save that froze on 553 loaded and played): loading a save releases the game's
4 GB arenas and reserves them again at the same bases. On 553 the JIT pool
records of the code the game had made executable in the old arenas outlived
the release; the new arena's pages stayed read-only and the game froze
([alias-tomb], [store-noalias], logs 11:21:36 and 11:22:59).
env.MADEIRA_ALIAS_RELEASE drops them with the arena (15 dropped on 555).
Version 6 (owner, 2026-10-16: the last known settings, kept while the game is
set aside): the lines of the owner's run on build 558 (log RiftApart.exe
15:58:00), which loaded the save and played.
- vram-mb 2048 and swap-mb 1024 are the values the owner ran from 553 on.
swap-mb 1024 and 8192 gave the same memory; 8192 only writes more to flash.
- env.MADEIRA_VA_PRESSURE_GAP_OK: with the app image high, a slow scan no longer
latches address-space pressure. 15:58 has 8 "not latched", 0 [steer] and a
5.45 GB peak; 13:23 without it had 15 [steer], a 6.9 GB peak and 2.4-2.8 GB
compressed.
- fence-early: no fps change was measured, and two runs went well with it.
Known open problems, not solved by this list: flat textures on large surfaces,
and 5-16 fps once iOS clamps the power.

(CrossOver 23.7+: "fully playable" with D3DMetal; one DXMT report on an M1 was
stuttery). Neither needs a launch option for it; -nojoy (no joystick polling) is
the one tip seen, and it is anecdotal. It needs the Steam client, as every library
Steam game here. No swap and no video-memory lines until a run shows a need.

config: # Reset to Recommended, at the bottom of the game's settings, brings them back.
notes: Breakneck (Steam 432940), an old 32-bit Unity game (its own mono.dll), through Madeira
Dock; the owner's runs on build 562 (2026-10-17, Send Log JW195K and 47GP93). Mono's
JIT keeps its code in 1 MB RWX chunks and patches it with unaligned atomic swaps. With
MADEIRA_WOW_RWX_PLAIN unset such a chunk is pool-aliased; the store emulator refuses
an unaligned atomic, FEX's own store faults again and the pool page never turns
writable, so one swap faulted until the redelivery guard ended the app. As plain
memory the swap lands (ml1279; its automatic mode only knows Wine Mono, not Unity's).
Build 563, owner: with the line the game runs well.

rules.title: No Rest for the Wicked
config: # BCD's recommended settings for No Rest for the Wicked.
# Reset to Recommended, at the bottom of the game's settings, brings them back.
notes: No Rest for the Wicked (Steam 1371980), build 574, iPhone18,1 (Send Log 0M4SJD): played at up to 60 fps for
about 100 s, then "FEXAlloc could not allocate" and exit 0xc000001d. The game (Unity IL2CPP) reserved 24
ranges of 511 MB; the steer valve put 23 of them in the emulator's 16 GB range (11.7 GB of it) and no 4 MB-
aligned gap was left for the emulator, which held 3.8 GB at the first refusal and 4.0 GB 4500 lines later.
env.MADEIRA_FEX_BAND_KEEP_MB = 6144 (build 576) keeps the lowest 6 GB of that range for the emulator; the
reservations that no longer fit go to the range below it. Not tried on a device yet.
Build 576, iPhone18,1 (Send Log 2NW5PY, 2026-10-21): with that line the game presents (654 frames at 30 s, 4021
at 150 s of the wait) and then its footprint climbs to 8.05 GB of the 8.19 GB limit during a texture
streaming burst from about 90 s (the game's textures 2.1 -> 7.4 GB requested, Metal's allocation 1.3 -> 3.2 GB,
compressed memory 1.7 -> 3.3 GB); from 120 s it presents 2 frames a second and the player closed it at 150 s.
7,816 of its textures are block-compressed, default-usage and shader-resource-only, with up to 14 levels; they
hold most of the 1.71 GB of block-compressed data (0.68 GB before the burst), and this GPU takes BC as it is.
dxmt = d3d11.mipClampBC=1 (build 577) drops the top level of each of them, three quarters of their bytes:
about 1.2 GB less at the end of that log. God of War's list uses the same option (its 4.0 GB of textures became
1.05 GB in a 2026-09-29 run). Not tried on a device yet.
Version 3 (2026-10-22): env.MADEIRA_WINTYPES = 1 (build 575). Auto-tune added it to this game (Send Log 3HSD2T, build 578, L30:
"trying wintypes-dll-optin", a rule that fires on an "import_dll Library api-ms-win-core-winrt-robuffer-l1-1-0.dll ... not found"
of the session before) and kept it (D6F1RA, build 578, L28; X6AVFR and 2PJS96, build 579). With it Wine's own wintypes.dll is linked
("MADEIRA_WINTYPES=1: wintypes.dll -> wintypes-optin.dll", X6AVFR L227) and the game plays 83 to 107 s, 2,264 to 5,625 frames, to its
own stop (an object header with an odd low bit, "[badrip]"), which no line here fixes. The list gives the first start the line.
Version 4 (2026-10-24): env.MADEIRA_CTX_FRAME = 1 (build 598). Send Logs GGFKAY and RKZSCQ (build 592, iPhone18,1) stop at the same "[badrip]"
(GGFKAY L40884, RKZSCQ L62769), and both stops come within 70 to 94 log lines of a stop-the-world: the game's garbage collector calls
NtGetContextThread on its stopped threads ("[ec-getctx] ml715", GGFKAY L40808-L40814 and L16234-L16265 and L29783-L29817, RKZSCQ L62675-
L62686, L16133-L16164 and L50964-L50997), and every answer is the thread's Mach-O state (is_ec=0, native_pc 0x2501e8ae8 in the system
library's wait, rsp a host thread stack 0x14c93fa00..0x15894fa00), not its x64 registers and stack; the server's own saved x64 context
was empty for most ("[srv-getctx] ml715" rip=0x0). A collector that cannot see the registers and stack of a parked thread frees what only
that thread holds, and the next use is an object whose first word is the free list's pointer (odd low bit). The same order holds in 31
logs of eight Unity titles (IL2CPP: this one, Megabonk, Vampire Survivors, Lonely Mountains, 1000xRESIST, Tape to Tape; Mono, which has the
same collector: Subnautica, Oxygen Not Included): the last NtGetContextThread burst comes 12 to 36 lines before the "[badrip]" in 22 of the
22 non-No-Rest logs and 68 to 212 lines before it in 8 of this game's 9 (one 936). The line makes the server report a thread parked in a
system call by its saved call frame ("[ctx-frame] ml716" lines say when); it was never run on a device. Off, nothing changes.

config: # BCD's recommended settings for Unrailed! 2: Back on Track.
# Reset to Recommended, at the bottom of the game's settings, brings them back.
notes: Unrailed! 2: Back on Track (Steam 2211170), build 576, iPhone18,2 (Send Log CR8H6H): Bootstrap.exe, a .NET 7+ runtime
(Godot), stops at start with "GC heap initialization failed with error 0x8007000E" (E_OUTOFMEMORY) and "Failed to
create CoreCLR" (L28803-28817). The .NET 7+ GC reserves a range of virtual memory for its regions heap when it starts,
256 GB by default; the log's request is 0x3fd2d28000 (261421 MB), and BCD's map has no such gap: "[mmap-place] ml1027
NO GAP FITS ... largest gap 32768 MB", "[jumbo] kernel-pick reserve failed (0xc0000017)" (L28741-28742). Microsoft
documents DOTNET_GCRegionRange (hexadecimal bytes, .NET 7 and later) for exactly this E_OUTOFMEMORY; its advice is two to
five times the heap's committed size, or twice the physical memory the process has when that is unknown. BCD reports at
most 8 GB to a process ("ml992: clamping reported physical memory 11722 MB -> 8192 MB"), so 400000000 = 16 GB; it fits the
32 GB gap and is only reserved, never committed. DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimit would size the range too but also limits what the
GC may commit, which changes its behaviour; not used. The line needs build 579: older builds' policy for downloaded lists
does not know the name. What follows the GC start is unknown; the next stop may be the CLR's write-barrier assert
(Quaver's), for which auto-tune has its rule dotnet-wx-off. The rule has no programs: Bootstrap.exe is too generic a
name, so a copy outside Steam is not matched. Not tried on a device yet.

threads ("PoolThread"), reads a 29882-byte file, FEX takes a 128 MB code buffer, and the game calls ExitProcess(1) ("NtTerminateProcess ... exit_code=0x1") after

Services SDK that is started without the launcher's sign-in arguments usually ends itself at once; this one is the first suspect.

configureLaunch, so this game's start really goes through BCD Host (the first time any Epic game does): the host asks Epic for the exchange code and
starts the game with Epic's full launcher arguments (BCDEpicStart.swift). The log then says "[epic-launch] host start held" and "[bcd-host] last
run" with numbers instead of "[bcd-host] no report"; the 32-bit game runs as a child of the 64-bit host. Not proven that this is the cause.
The other four lines are diagnostics: MADEIRA_GUEST_LOG = all mirrors the game's own text logs (UE3's Launch.log with the reason) into BCD's
log, MADEIRA_FILE_TRACE lists the files it opens. Only this list and the Danganronpa list carry the first two. The Steam copy of the game has no

rules.title: LEGO Batman: The Videogame
config: # BCD's recommended settings for LEGO Batman: The Videogame.
# Reset to Recommended, at the bottom of the game's settings, brings them back.
notes: LEGO Batman: The Videogame (Steam 21000, LEGOBatman.exe, 32-bit Direct3D 9, BCD Dock), build 592, iPad17,4 (Send Logs T8H0E1 and KMSZ3M, 2026-10-23):
the game runs (55-58 fps, 1112x832 fullscreen, no D3D9 warning or error, no exception) but the picture is wrong: mostly black with a few white shapes
and light cones (the tester's screenshot; the tester says Madeira showed the same). Nothing in either log names the cause. One fact is new: the game compiles
its HLSL at run time. d3dx9_35.dll (Wine's builtin: it loads d3dcompiler_47.dll) calls D3DCompile2 222 times in each session ("vkd3d:00ac:fixme:
D3DCompile2VKD3D Ignoring flags 0x1200", KMSZ3M L9686-L11173, during the first 1000 presents), so every shader the game draws with comes from
vkd3d-shader's HLSL compiler and Wine's constant table, not from Microsoft's. Wine's builtin d3dx9_35 is built --prefer-native, so a copy written by the
game's DirectX setup would have been loaded instead: DXSETUP ended with status 0 in both sessions ("directx=0", T8H0E1 L50) and still the builtin is
in use, so that setup installed nothing the loader found. Of ~1250 logs only this game and LEGO Batman 2 (BXW23W, 328 compiles) call the compiler.
The accepted bytecode raises no "DXSO ..." error.
Diagnostic lines only, from build 598, no rendering change: MADEIRA_FRAME_STATS = 1 (one [frame] line a second: GPU busy, passes and attachments
per frame); MADEIRA_GPU_TRACE = 20,2,1 (one frame 20 s after the first present, encoder by encoder: attachments with format, size, load and store
action, draw counts, the Metal function of each draw); DXMT_DUMP_D9_SHADER = 1 (one line per created shader: model, instruction count, samplers,
kill, derivatives); WINEDEBUG +loaddll (one line per loaded module: whether d3dx9_35.dll is Wine's or the one DirectX's setup wrote). vkd3d's own

trace (VKD3D_DEBUG=trace) would print the compiler's messages but also the IR of every pass of 222 shaders: too much for a list. Experiments the tester can add by hand on build 592, one at a time: env.MADEIRA_RP_LOAD = 1, then
env.DXMT_D9_SCENE_BATCH = 0, env.DXMT_CLEAR_DISCARD_STORE = 0, env.DXMT_D9_SHADER_PRUNE = 0 with env.DXMT_D9_BINDING_PRUNE = 0, and Settings >
Graphics > Direct3D 9 > Native ARM64. No auto-tune rule: the session counts as played, so auto-tune never looks at it.

rules.title: Glyphica: Typing Survival
config: # BCD's recommended settings for Glyphica: Typing Survival.
# Reset to Recommended, at the bottom of the game's settings, brings them back.
notes: Glyphica: Typing Survival (Steam 2400160, neosphere.exe: the Sphere engine neoSphere with ChakraCore.dll, 64-bit, ARM64EC, an OpenGL and Direct3D 9 importer),
build 592, iPad16,3, two Send Logs of one start (777YHV and JAHWGD, 2026-10-24): the process ends 0.8 s after Wine starts with exit c0000602
(STATUS_FAIL_FAST_EXCEPTION) from RaiseFailFastException inside ChakraCore.dll while it loads, before the game's own code runs (stage 2, "crashed at stage 2
after 2 s"). The caller is ChakraCore's static constructor GlobalSecurityPolicy (lib/Common/Core/GlobalSecurityPolicy.cpp, ChakraCore 1.11): it loads
api-ms-win-core-memory-l1-1-3.dll, calls GetProcessMitigationPolicy( ProcessControlFlowGuardPolicy ) into a local it never cleared and reads
EnableControlFlowGuard from it; when that bit is set it looks up SetProcessValidCallTargets, which this Wine does not export, and fails fast. The log shows
the call ("fixme:process:GetProcessMitigationPolicy (FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, 7, <stack>, 4): stub") and, the next line, the unhandled exception c0000602;
Wine's stub answers TRUE and writes nothing, so the answer was whatever the stack held.
env.MADEIRA_ZERO_MITIGATION_POLICY = 1 (build 600; the Wine fork's kernelbase process.c) makes the stub zero the structure (no mitigation is enabled), so
ChakraCore takes its non-CFG path. Off: the stub as before. Only this list and auto-tune's rule chakracore-cfg-policy-failfast set it. Not proven on a device:
what the game does after ChakraCore starts is unknown (neoSphere's display may ask for OpenGL, which BCD does not have; ChakraCore's JIT runs under FEX).

notes: The Adventures of Elliot: The Millennium Tales (Steam 3483510, Unreal Engine, Denuvo): Elliot-Win64-Shipping.exe is 473 MiB with its relocations stripped,
so it can only load at 0x140000000. A BCD log (8Q0SJ8, build 592, iPad17,4, a copy outside Steam started through Elliot.exe) shows the 128 MB window and the
image (size 0x1d91c000, charact 0x23) overlapping the JIT pool: "failed to create main module ... c0000018", exit 0xc0000018 after 2 s.
exe-window-mb = 480 keeps the window for the whole image (the 16 MB step that holds it). The window leaves no single 896 MB run for the pool, and the
image copy in that log already used 505 of the pool's 592 MB, so env.MADEIRA_X64_IMAGE_NOCOPY = 1 (the image is not copied; BCD's other lists for large
fixed-base programs have it) comes with it. pool-split = 1, pool-low = 1 and pool-low-margin = 32 are the pool settings this game was reported
to play with on an iPhone 17 Pro at 30 fps; pool-above-window = 1 (the pool pairs the two runs above the window, 240 + 288 MB there, instead of the
higher one alone) and env.MADEIRA_KUSER_KEEP_REGS = 1 (registers that only hold a KUSER-looking value are left alone after the sub-floor service: Denuvo
keeps 0x7ffe0283 in rcx while it reads KUSER through another register, and the TLS pointer it computed was off by the relocation) are the two changes
that report also depended on, which BCD has as switches. Not proven on a device in BCD. The rule and its lines carry minBuild 602 (the switches are read from that build).
A copy outside Steam started through Elliot.exe (the log above) is not matched by this rule; auto-tune's exe-window-fixed-base proposes the window there.
